acceptanceCriteria: Each listed format is parsed into an instruction row that carries its declared scope (glob or always) and is admitted only for subjects inside that scope.
Fixtures cover an in-scope and an out-of-scope subject for every format.
Unrecognized or malformed frontmatter produces an explicit uncertainty entry, not silent omission.
body: Filed 2026-09-27 from the owner-requested gap analysis of Corvint against competing context tools, current standards and a trial on a local clone of MeVille (TypeScript, about 4,600 tracked files). `internal/contextindex/parse.go:197` classifies AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, copilot-instructions.md and `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md` as instructions, but no Go source reads the `applyTo` glob, so a path-scoped Copilot instruction is treated as repository-wide or not at all. Not recognized: `.cursor/rules/*.mdc` (alwaysApply / globs / description modes), `.kiro/steering/*.md`, `.windsurf/rules`, `.clinerules`, Codex `AGENTS.override.md`, and `@path` imports inside CLAUDE.md. Users expect existing rules to just work (Cursor docs rules; GitHub custom-instructions reference). Each format is project-owned authority whose scope is data, so it fits invariant 3 without new spec language.
title: context: recognize scoped instruction formats with their activation scope (applyTo, Cursor .mdc, Kiro steering, Windsurf/Cline rules, AGENTS.override.md, CLAUDE.md @imports)
